title: Learning practical tricks from retired players
summary: Punch and Zango talk about professors versus practical tips, and Punch says retired players share most.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Moose, if you think of any questions about trumpet playing, go ahead and ask them.
Well, I guess that's the man they ask, huh? Yeah. You've been a lot longer than me.
All right. Ain't like them professors, you know. Some of them questions I can answer, but take a man like Joe Hodden and he can answer more than anything he asks.
Well, I tell you, I'm lucky I can read the name on the top of a sheet of music, much less the notes.
There's a lot of practical things that you're not going to get from professors, you know. That's...
A lot of little tricks that different guys have, you know, that make for that jazz.
Well, I don't know, I think after a fellow has retired, he'll show you more than anything. But if he's still playing, he'll show you everything, you can catch up with him, you know.
